question: Can neural networks judge the grammatical acceptability of single English sentences, and how far are they from human judgments?
contributions: Introduce CoLA, 10k+ linguistics-literature sentences with expert acceptability labels
Train semi-supervised neural sequence models on CoLA and compare with unsupervised Lau et al. (2016) models
Analyse impact of training data domain and quantity
Assess performance on specific linguistic phenomena

method.summary: Builds CoLA from example sentences in linguistics publications with Boolean acceptability labels, with in-domain and out-of-domain splits. Baselines are BiLSTM max-pooling classifiers over BNC/GloVe/ELMo-style embeddings, optionally with encoders pretrained on a real/fake sentence discrimination task, plus Lau et al. (2016) LM-threshold models and a CBOW baseline; evaluated by accuracy and MCC against a small human study.

datasets.name: CoLA
datasets.split: in-domain: train 8551, dev 527, test 530 (17 sources); out-of-domain: dev 516, test 533 (6 sources); 1049 OOD total
datasets.source: Examples from 23 linguistics publications (Table 2); downloadable from nyu-mll.github.io/CoLA; part of GLUE
datasets.preprocessing: Excluded unacceptable pragmatic anomalies, unavailable meanings, prescriptive rules, nonce words; non-Boolean labels '?'/'#' dropped, '??'/'*?' set unacceptable (<3% of cases); alternates expanded; vocabulary restricted to 100k most frequent BNC words by manual edits; fragments completed into sentences

datasets.name: British National Corpus (BNC)
datasets.preprocessing: lowercased, tokenized with NLTK, 100k most frequent words kept, others <unk>

datasets.name: Real/fake data
datasets.size: entire BNC plus an equal amount of fake data
datasets.source: Fake = samples from the LSTM LM, or BNC sentences with a subset of words randomly permuted

datasets.name: Targeted test sets (SVO, Wh-extraction, causative-inchoative, subject-verb agreement, reflexive)
datasets.size: SVO 100 triples x 5 permutations; Wh 260 pairs; Causative 91 verb/object pairs (36 alternate, 55 not); SV agreement 169 quadruples; Reflexive 144 sentences (1 in 6 acceptable)
datasets.source: Generated with rewrite grammars (inspired by Ettinger et al. 2016)

models.name: Pooling classifier (best: ELMo-style, real/fake encoder, CoLA classifier)
models.architecture: deep BiLSTM encoder, concatenated fwd/bwd states, max-pooling, then sigmoid (optionally one tanh hidden layer)
models.init_from: encoder pretrained on real/fake task, frozen
models.hidden: embedding 819, real/fake encoder hidden 528, acceptability classifier hidden 1134

models.name: Lau et al. (2016) LM + Word LogProb Min-1 metric with fitted threshold
models.architecture: LSTM LM and 2/3/4-gram LMs trained on BNC

models.name: CBOW
models.architecture: sum of BNC embeddings into one-hidden-layer MLP

training.objective: LM likelihood; real/fake binary discrimination; CoLA binary acceptability
training.lr: random search in [3e-3, 1e-5] for LM and end-to-end classifiers; [1e-2, 1e-5] for transfer classifiers
training.epochs: LM: up to 7 days or until 4 epochs without dev perplexity improvement; real/fake: up to 7 days or 4 epochs without dev MCC gain; CoLA transfer classifiers: until 20 epochs without dev MCC gain
training.seeds: 20 restarts per config for design experiments

other.random_search: 20 LSTM LMs; 20 pooling classifiers end-to-end each for BNC, GloVe, ELMo-style real/fake; 20 end-to-end on CoLA; transfer: 5 best encoders per embedding type x 10 classifiers

inference.samples: best run per experiment reported in Table 4; 20 restarts averaged in Tables 5 and Fig 4

parameters.lau_threshold: threshold fitted by 10-fold cross-validation on the CoLA test set

metrics.name: MCC
metrics.definition: Matthews correlation coefficient, Pearson r for Boolean variables; 0 for unrelated predictions regardless of class imbalance

limits: Absolute model performance far below human (MCC 0.341 vs 0.695 in-domain); only LSTM-era models tested, no Transformers or BERT
Lau et al. threshold is fit with 10-fold CV on the test labels
Table 4 reports the best run per experiment, not mean; no significance tests
Labels are published linguists' judgments; 13% of CoLA labels contradict majority human judgment; 1-2% have PDF character-recognition errors
Boolean single-sentence task, not minimal pairs; dialect and missing-context effects
Authors concede CoLA may have biases that other annotation schemes would detect; excludes pragmatic/meaning-dependent unacceptability
Targeted test sets are small synthetic sets; authors speculate underrepresentation of agreement in CoLA explains poor results

terms.definition: determined by introspective judgments of native speakers, as opposed to grammaticality, which is determined by a grammatical formalism
Matthews correlation coefficient, a special case of Pearson's r for Boolean variables
